classification.difficultyReason: Introduce a radius to an upper square vertex and recognise perpendicular lengths s and s/2; use Pythagoras to obtain the square's area, then subtract it from the semicircle area.

content.prompt: The vertices of a square lie on the boundary of a semicircle of radius $10\text{ cm}$. Find the shaded area shown in terms of $\pi$.

spec.description: Semicircle with a square centred on its diameter. Both lower square vertices lie on the diameter and both upper vertices lie on the arc. Light purple identifies all of the semicircle outside the square, including the cap above it. A red point marks the diameter midpoint.
spec.mathematics: Drawing radius 2; square half-side 2/sqrt(5) and side 4/sqrt(5), ensuring each upper vertex lies on the semicircle. Physical radius 10 cm is supplied in the stem.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated lengths, construction lines or answers appear in the question diagram.

answer.short:
$(50\pi-80)\text{ cm}^2$

Use Pythagoras to find the square's area, then subtract it from the semicircle's area.
answer.worked:
Let the square have side length $s$ cm. Join the centre of the semicircle to an upper vertex of the square. This gives a right-angled triangle with perpendicular sides $s$ and $\frac{s}{2}$, and hypotenuse $10$.
$$\begin{align*}s^2+\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)^2&=10^2\\\frac54s^2&=100\\s^2&=80\\A_{\text{square}}&=80\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{semicircle}}&=\frac12\pi(10)^2\\A_{\text{semicircle}}&=50\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=(50\pi-80)\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
